But the tokenizer throws away characters that carry meaning (sign, comparator, approximation, non-ASCII letters, decimal comma, superscripts, unit or currency after a space), so fabrications that differ only in those characters come out supported. Probes: REVF-H8a7-probe/attack.py, REVF-H8a7-probe/runs/e2e.

issues.problem: Signs, comparators and approximation marks are dropped as punctuation, so a fabricated sign or bound reaches 'supported'.
issues.evidence: Each claim <= quote pair below is supported: 'Net margin was 12% in 2023.' <= 'Net margin was -12% in 2023.'; 'Q3 revenue was -5% ...' <= '+5%'; 'Temperature can reach 40°C' <= '−40°C'; 'Latency is > 5 ms' <= '< 5 ms'; 'Throughput is ≤ 10 Gbps' <= '≥ 10 Gbps'; 'Revenue was $5m' <= '~$5m'; 'Throughput is 10 Gbps' <= '≈ 10 Gbps'. End to end with verify --strict: status pass, exit 0.
issues.suggested_fix: Make a leading -, U+2212 or + part of the figure token, and make <, >, ≤, ≥, ~, ≈ and ± tokens of their own. Better: any character that is not a letter, digit, whitespace or plain sentence punctuation must match exactly.

issues.problem: Letters outside a-z are dropped. Names that differ only in an accented letter count as equal, and claims in non-Latin scripts reduce to their figures alone.
issues.evidence: 'Müller was appointed CEO in 2021.' <= 'Möller was appointed CEO in 2021.' supported (end to end, exit 0). 'Выручка выросла на 40% в 2023 году.' <= 'Выручка упала на 40% ...' supported ('rose' vs 'fell'). '营收增长40%' <= '营收下降40%' supported.
issues.suggested_fix: Tokenize Unicode letters ([^\W\d_]+) instead of [a-z]. Or, at the least, return needs_review when either text holds letters the tokenizer would drop.

issues.problem: Every comma inside a number is taken as a thousands separator, so a European decimal comma becomes a 10x or 100x figure.
issues.evidence: 'The fee is €15 million per year.' <= '€1,5 million' supported; 'The plan costs €350 per month.' <= '€3,50' supported.
issues.suggested_fix: Strip a comma only when exactly three digits follow it (\d{1,3}(,\d{3})+). Any other comma inside a number keeps the token distinct or sends the claim to needs_review.

issues.evidence: '10⁶ requests' <= '106 requests' (NFKC turns the superscript into a digit); 'fell to 40 in March' <= '40 % in March' (a % after a space is dropped); '50 $ per seat' <= '50 € per seat' (a currency symbol after the number is dropped); 'ships in 45' <= 'twenty twenty-five' (a year in words is summed to 45).
issues.suggested_fix: Map superscripts before NFKC, or flag them. Attach a % or currency symbol that follows a space. Stop summing a tens word followed by another tens word, so 'twenty twenty-five' is not 45.

issues.problem: Honest claims are 'contradicted', and --strict exits 1. Figures with the same value in another format count as different. The check also accepts one or more differing figures, although the binding rule and SKILL.md say one. With that, a sibling quote from the same source about another year contradicts an honest claim.
issues.evidence: Contradicted: 'Version 3 shipped in May.' <= 'Version 3.0 ...' (end to end, exit 1); '$5' <= '$5.00'; '.95' <= '0.95'; '40%' <= '40.0%'; '90s' <= '1990s'; "'24" <= '2024'. Quotes ['Revenue was $5m in 2023.', 'Revenue rose to $7m in 2024.'] make the claim 'Revenue was $7m in 2024.' contradicted; likewise 'Acme had 150 staff in 2023.' against sibling-year quotes.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat numerically equal figures as equal (compare float values within the same shape). Require exactly one differing figure. Send abbreviated years and decades to needs_review.

issues.location: SKILL.md vs reference/quality-gates.md 'What makes a claim contradicted'
issues.problem: The two docs disagree. SKILL.md and the quality-gates table say 'one exact figure replaced'; the quality-gates bullet and the code say 'one or more figures'. Separately, the docs list two aliases, but ALIASES also maps are->is and am->is.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the docs with the code once the figure rule is fixed, and document the are/am/is pairs.

issues.problem: this/that and its/their are dropped, so 'that year' matches 'this year' and 'Their revenue' matches 'Its revenue'. The referent changes. This is documented as intended filler.
issues.evidence: 'Revenue doubled that year.' <= 'Revenue doubled this year.' supported.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider keeping the demonstratives and possessives as words.
